title: Skybox Files $550M Fourth Data Center in Hutto as Texas Tightens Grid Rules
key_facts: Skybox and Prologis filed with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation for a fourth data center at their Hutto campus, 28 miles northeast of Austin.
$550 million, 846,300 sq ft single-story building; construction January 2027 to October 2028.
Filing first reported by Data Center Dynamics.
The campus is planned to deliver 600 MW of IT capacity; Oncor and LCRA are building two 300 MW substations nearby.
On 21 Sep Gov. Greg Abbott directed a freeze on environmental and air permits for data centers pending grid and water audits.
On 18 Sep the Public Utility Commission adopted a rule requiring loads of 75 MW or more to post $50,000 per megawatt before grid studies.
quote_evidence: The $550 million project, dubbed Skybox Hutto 4, is slated for construction between January 2027 and October 2028, and it would be the largest of the four buildings the company has proposed in the city so far.
The regulation stems from Senate Bill 6, enacted to protect retail electric ratepayers from stranded transmission infrastructure costs, according to White & Case LLP.
why_it_matters_hint: A big new filing arrives just as Texas tightens permit and grid-security rules.
event_date: filing date not stated; reported 5 Oct 2026
notes: Hoodline relays Data Center Dynamics and other outlets; Hoodline itself says it is unclear whether the new rules will apply to Hutto 4.
